doc.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

chapter: Listening, jazz history and the future
title: Getting a band into the Blue Note
summary: Rivello says bands may have to pay to play and mentions other places in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Speaking of going to New York with a band, how the heck do you get into the Blue Note with your band?
That I don’t know, on an off night and you pay I guess.

Well occasionally there are the periods where you have to buy the room and you invite the critics or you invite the audience or you do the ticket sales. So — the Blue Note I don’t know. I think you have to be a Chick Corea or somebody — maybe he has to pay. But there’s plenty of other places that people are paying attention to. So we’ll see what happens with that, but that’s definitely on the front burner.
